stem:
Lalit checks which expression must always be even for integer values of the letters. He compares 4m + 2q with x^2 + 2.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: 4m + 2q is always even, because it equals 2(2m + q).
x^2 + 2 is always even, because the constant 2 is even.
An expression is even only when the letters themselves are even.
x^2 + 2 is always even whenever 4m + 2q is even, with no further check.

teacher.key_rationale: 4m + 2q = 2(2m + q) is always even for integers m, q. x^2 + 2 fails when x is odd, so claiming it from the constant alone is the excluded case. Requiring letters to be even omits that the factored form works for any integers. Tying x^2 + 2 to 4m + 2q reverses the separate checks.

mx_swap.reason: Divisibility-of-sums CWO invents M+N language not in the stem; kept scope_error, condition_omission, relationship_reversal on the always-even hinge.
